paper.title: Typical Superpositions are Magical
paper.authors: Joshuah T. Heath, Andrew Urilyon, Damien Quinn, Graham Kells
paper.abstract: The non-stabilizerness, or "magic", of a quantum state is a common metric for the hardness of simulation on a classical computer, and is often quantified by the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE). We show how random superpositions of classically simulable states saturate the SRE to the symmetry-restricted Haar-random maximum. For any large-$N$ random pure-state ensemble satisfying the conditions of Schur's lemma, the average SRE of the $m$-component superposition $\langle M_2(m)\rangle=N-\log_2[\langle W(m)\rangle]$ is governed by an average witness $\langle W(m)\rangle$ that universally decomposes into a Haar floor and an ensemble-specific excess. As the number of components $m$ increases, the excess is suppressed, resulting in a logarithmic scaling of the SRE before plateauing at the Haar-valued maximum. We derive a general closed form for $\langle W(m)\rangle$ in the thermodynamic limit, and numerically verify our result for random stabilizer states and random Gaussian states.

2610.22476.abstract_translated: 量子状態の非安定化性、または「魔法性」は、古典コンピュータ上でのシミュレーションの難しさの一般的な指標であり、安定化レニーエントロピー（SRE）によって定量化されることが多い。我々は、古典的にシミュレーション可能な状態のランダムな重ね合わせが、SREを対称性制限ハールランダム最大値まで飽和させる方法を示す。シューアの補題の条件を満たす任意の大きな$N$ランダム純粋状態アンサンブルに対して、$m$成分重ね合わせ$\langle M_2(m)\rangle=N-\log_2[\langle W(m)\rangle]$の平均SREは、ハールフロアとアンサンブル固有の過剰に普遍的に分解される平均証拠$\langle W(m)\rangle$によって支配される。成分数 $m$ が増加するにつれて、過剰分は抑制され、SRE は対数的に増加した後、ハール値の最大値でプラトーに達します。我々は、熱力学的極限における $\langle W(m)\rangle$ の一般的な閉形式を導出し、ランダム安定化状態とランダムガウス状態について数値的に結果を検証します。

paper.title: Exploring Quantum Phase Transitions Beyond Landau Theory on a Quantum Processor
paper.authors: Ruizhe Shen, Yin Zhong, Ching Hua Lee
paper.abstract: Direct continuous quantum phase transitions between phases that break distinct symmetries challenge the conventional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm and provide a framework for deconfined quantum criticality. Here, we investigate a Landau-forbidden ferromagnetic-to-valence-bond-solid (FM-VBS) transition in a frustrated one-dimensional spin chain using superconducting quantum processors. Combining matrix-product-state-assisted circuit preparation with quantum-hardware measurements, we resolve the suppression of long-range ferromagnetic correlations and the redistribution of competing-order fluctuations across the transition. Distance-resolved correlations and finite-size analyses reveal signatures consistent with critical behavior. We further extend our investigation to nonequilibrium dynamics, directly preparing dimerized states and tracking the evolution of VBS order and joint FM-VBS fluctuations under local unitary interactions. Our results establish a versatile quantum-hardware framework for probing competing orders, critical correlations, and many-body dynamics beyond conventional Landau theory.

2610.22482.abstract_translated: 異なる対称性を破る相間の直接的な連続量子相転移は、従来のランダウ・ギンツブルグ・ウィルソン・パラダイムに挑戦し、非閉じ込め量子臨界性の枠組みを提供する。本研究では、超伝導量子プロセッサを用いて、フラストレーションのある一次元スピン鎖におけるランダウ法則で禁じられている強磁性体から価電子結合固体（FM-VBS）への相転移を調査する。行列積状態支援回路準備と量子ハードウェア測定を組み合わせることで、相転移全体にわたる長距離強磁性相関の抑制と競合する秩序変動の再分配を解明する。距離分解相関と有限サイズ解析により、臨界挙動と一致する特徴が明らかになる。さらに、非平衡ダイナミクスに調査を拡張し、二量体化状態を直接準備し、局所的なユニタリー相互作用の下でのVBS秩序とFM-VBS結合変動の進化を追跡する。我々の研究結果は、従来のランダウ理論を超えて、競合する秩序、臨界相関、多体ダイナミクスを調査するための、汎用性の高い量子ハードウェアの枠組みを確立するものである。

paper.title: Multi-Time States in Quantum and Operational Probabilistic Theories: An Axiomatic Framework
paper.authors: Kaumudibikash Goswami, Archana Barvar, Manabendra Nath Bera
paper.abstract: Quantum states over time were introduced, in part, to extend Bayesian probability to quantum theory and have since found applications across diverse areas, ranging from quantum causality and open-system dynamics to tests of macroscopic realism. While axiomatic characterizations of these states exist for Markovian dynamics, a general framework accommodating non-Markovian dynamics is still lacking. Moreover, extending this framework beyond quantum mechanics to general physical theories also remains elusive. In this work, we develop an axiomatic framework for multi-time states within a class of operational probabilistic theories (OPTs) that includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Based on three assumptions---compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency---the framework accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics, and provides sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory within OPT. As a concrete application of our OPT framework, we fully characterize the unique multi-time state in boxworld and develop a method for Bayesian retrodiction of physical transformations there. Our general framework is consistent with quantum theory, reproducing several existing results. In the non-Markovian quantum dynamics, we establish a correspondence between multi-time states and the process-matrix framework, and fully characterize the multi-time states compatible with general dynamics. This correspondence also lets us infer quantum causal models from multi-time states, and as a proof of principle, we propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order from quantum multi-time states. These results provide a unified framework for studying spatio-temporal states, causal relations, and Bayesian reasoning within OPTs, with implications for both fundamental and applied research.

paper.title: Resonant pair production and flat band melting in a driven Rydberg chain
paper.authors: Tista Banerjee, K. Sengupta
paper.abstract: We study a Rydberg chain subjected to a two-tone periodic drive of the detuning $\Delta(t)$ and Rabi frequency $\Omega(t)$ at frequencies $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2=\nu \omega_1$ respectively with $\nu \in \mathbf{Z}$. In the strong Rydberg blockade limit, such a system reduces to the PXP model and exhibits exact Floquet flat band. Here we determine, using a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, the domain of validity of such PXP dynamics once the blockade-violating processes are taken into account. We study the melting of such flat bands in the presence of strong, but finite, blockade strength. Using Floquet perturbation theory (FPT), we identify two mechanisms for such melting; the first occurs due to the presence of many-body resonances involving resonant production of nearest-neighbor Rydberg excitation pairs while the second involves virtual processes that access intermediate states with such pairs. Our analytical FPT results match with those obtained using exact diagonalization on a finite chain. We study the dynamics for $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ (Fock state with no Rydberg excitation), $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$, and $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ (Fock states with Rydberg excitations on alternate and every third site respectively) initial states. We find that $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ shows exceptional stability against resonant pair formation while $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ exhibits flat band melting via virtual processes away from the direct resonances. We find oscillatory dynamics with large time period for the $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$ initial state and the presence of Floquet scars that have large overlap with $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ state; these phenomena occur due to processes that are absent in the PXP limit. We propose measurement of nearest neighbor pair correlation functions using Rydberg atom quantum simulator platforms as an accessible experimental probe for these effects.

paper.title: A thermally and perturbatively stable classical spin model in two dimensions
paper.authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, Ting-Chun Lin, Ryan Thorngren
paper.abstract: We show that the 2D classical spin model constructed in arXiv:2605.10943 hosts many metastable states at non-zero temperature which are stable to arbitrary Hamiltonian perturbations, providing the first such example. Our proof relies on a recursive application of the cluster expansion.

paper.title: Circuit Synthesis for Variational Quantum Algorithms: The Depth of Algebra and Geometry
paper.authors: Boris Tsvelikhovskiy
paper.abstract: The analysis of Hamiltonian Variational Ans\"atze centers on three fundamental questions: which states are exactly reachable from a given initial state, what native control depth suffices for local and global synthesis, and whether a bounded circuit extension can expose a direction of decreasing cost at a suboptimal output. We address these challenges by leveraging the dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) associated with the circuits and the geometry of the initial state's orbit under the action of the corresponding dynamical Lie group $G$. We show that an initial state has a closed projective orbit whenever it is a nondegenerate eigenstate of a control Hamiltonian. Combined with asymptotic QAOA convergence, this guarantees exact, finite depth ground state preparation for architectures employing diagonal problem Hamiltonians and irreducible stoquastic mixers. We bound the number of native control exponentials required for local unitary synthesis and state preparation using DLA commutator filtration growth alongside reachable orbit dimensions. Complementing these local results, we construct global frameworks on invariant sectors equipped with full unitary or special unitary dynamical Lie algebras. These constructions yield explicit applications to Pauli-generated systems and constrained maximum independent set multi-angle QAOA circuits; specifically, we show that their native control costs are directly determined by commutator filtration depth and independent-set toggle-group geometry, respectively. Finally, if the dynamical Lie group is compact, the observable $H_P$ generates an admissible evolution ($iH_P \in \mathfrak{g}$, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is the DLA), and the projective orbit of the initial state contains a ground state ray of $H_P$, then a bounded depth, identity-initialized circuit extension exhibits either first-order descent or negative curvature at every suboptimal circuit output.

paper.title: Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Solving Lindblad Master Equations
paper.authors: Rafael Florencio D\'iaz, Julio Guerrero Garc\'ia, Elvira Romera Guti\'errez
paper.abstract: Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a promising approach for simulating open quantum systems, yet their expressive power and trainability remain poorly understood. We propose a variational framework for solving Lindblad master equations by minimizing a residual cost function using a compositional ansatz obtained by combining a classical neural network with a parameterized quantum circuit. The density matrix is represented through a purification on an enlarged Hilbert space, ensuring positivity, Hermiticity, and unit trace by construction, while all gradients are evaluated exactly via the parameter-shift rule. Beyond the algorithmic formulation, we derive an upper bound for the covering number of the proposed compositional model and compare it with that of purely quantum neural networks. Our analysis shows that the classical parametrization enlarges the effective hypothesis class while providing finer control over its complexity, thereby establishing a theoretical connection between expressivity, covering numbers, effective dimension, and the barren plateau phenomenon. Numerical experiments validate both the accuracy of the proposed method for representative Lindblad master equations and the theoretical predictions regarding gradient concentration. These results provide a unified variational and theoretical framework for the simulation of dissipative quantum dynamics using compositional quantum machine learning models.

2610.22691.abstract_translated: 変分量子アルゴリズムは、開放量子システムのシミュレーションにおいて有望なアプローチとして注目されていますが、その表現力と学習可能性については十分に理解されていません。本稿では、古典ニューラルネットワークとパラメータ化された量子回路を組み合わせた構成的仮説を用いて残差コスト関数を最小化することで、リンドブラッドマスター方程式を解くための変分フレームワークを提案します。密度行列は、拡張されたヒルベルト空間上での精製によって表現され、構成上、正値性、エルミート性、単位トレースが保証されます。一方、すべての勾配はパラメータシフト規則によって正確に評価されます。アルゴリズムの定式化に加え、提案する構成モデルの被覆数の上限を導出し、純粋な量子ニューラルネットワークの被覆数と比較します。分析の結果、古典的パラメータ化によって有効仮説クラスが拡大し、その複雑さをより細かく制御できることが示され、表現力、被覆数、有効次元、および不毛なプラトー現象の間に理論的な関連性が確立されました。数値実験により、代表的なリンドブラッドマスター方程式に対する提案手法の精度と、勾配集中に関する理論的予測の両方が検証されました。これらの結果は、構成型量子機械学習モデルを用いた散逸量子力学のシミュレーションのための、統一的な変分法および理論的枠組みを提供する。

paper.title: Metric and Dispersive Dynamics of Phase Perturbations in Bohmian Quantum Mechanics
paper.authors: Felipe S. Esc\'orcio, Hermano Velten
paper.abstract: By linearizing the hydrodynamic equations associated with the Madelung transformation in the context of Bohmian dynamics, we derive an effective metric for the phase perturbation around a background state. We show that the metric previously obtained previously by the same authors arises naturally as a particular case of a more general structure, in which the complete functional variation of the quantum potential is retained and external classical potentials can be incorporated. This generalization preserves the dependence of the quantum potential on the density and its spatial derivatives, generating additional terms that introduce dispersive corrections and act as sources in the effective Klein-Gordon equation. To organize these contributions, we introduce differential operators that separate the local sector responsible for the effective geometry from the corrections associated with the complete functional structure of the quantum potential. We identify the conditions under which these additional terms become negligible, recovering homogeneous propagation and the effective geometry for the Gaussian wave packet of a free particle.

paper.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
paper.authors: M. Javad Zakeri, Alaric Pan, Darren D Hudson, Andrea Blanco-Redondo
paper.abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. We experimentally realize silicon photonic topological superlattices in which the nonlinear generation pathway itself becomes programmable via tailored excitations. The superlattices host a multiband manifold of co localized topological interface modes, while coherently controlled inputs synthesize pump superpositions within this protected basis. We showcase this principle by selectively addressing topological biphoton eigenstates, steering correlations to produce a desired target state in a high-dimensional Hilbert space, and inverse-designing pump states that generate targeted Schmidt dimensionalities. Site-resolved two-photon correlation measurements remain reproducible across nominally identical fabricated devices, demonstrating robustness to realistic nanofabrication-induced disorder. Programmable preparation of topological entangled states establishes a pathway towards exploiting topological photonic modes as application-specific quantum resources, enabling tailored input states for high-dimensional quantum communication, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing.

2610.22738.abstract_translated: 量子もつれ状態のプログラム可能な準備は、スケーラブルな量子情報処理、量子ネットワーク、およびフォトニック量子コンピューティングにとって中心的な要件です。トポロジカルフォトニックプラットフォームは、対称性で保護された光モードに情報を符号化することで、堅牢な量子状態生成への魅力的な道筋を提供しますが、生成されるもつれ状態は通常、格子形状によって決定されるため、プログラム可能性がありません。本稿では、集積フォトニック格子の非線形光ポンププロファイルを逆設計することにより、トポロジカルもつれ状態のプログラム可能な準備を実現します。このアプローチにより、生成されるもつれ状態の次元とモード構造の両方を決定論的に制御しながら、そのトポロジカル特性を維持できます。非線形生成経路自体が、調整された励起によってプログラム可能になるシリコンフォトニックトポロジカル超格子を実験的に実現しました。この超格子は、共局在するトポロジカル界面モードのマルチバンドマニホールドをホストし、コヒーレントに制御された入力によって、この保護された基底内でポンプ重ね合わせが合成されます。本研究では、トポロジカルな二光子固有状態を選択的に操作し、相関を制御して高次元ヒルベルト空間における所望のターゲット状態を生成し、さらにポンプ状態を逆設計することで、この原理を実証します。サイト分解された二光子相関測定は、名目上同一の製造デバイス間で再現性を維持しており、現実的なナノ加工に起因する不規則性に対する堅牢性を示しています。トポロジカルなもつれ状態のプログラム可能な準備により、トポロジカルなフォトニックモードをアプリケーション固有の量子リソースとして活用する道が開かれ、高次元量子通信、量子ネットワーク、およびフォトニック量子コンピューティング向けにカスタマイズされた入力状態が可能になります。

paper.title: The Classical Boundary of Quantum Computation: History-Resolved Causal Stochastic Machines and the Cost of Classicalization
paper.authors: Kyoungho Cho, Junghee Ryu, Minsu Kim, Jeongho Bang
paper.abstract: What separates quantum computation from classical computation when a classical model may retain every branch history and arbitrary causal memory? We study this question using history-resolved causal stochastic machines (HCSMs), which describe positive causal history laws. Probabilistic Turing machines (PTMs) embed in stochastic-ensemble models (SEnMs), which in turn embed in HCSMs. We prove that HCSM history laws coincide exactly with the fixed-basis, prefix-preserving diagonal sector of ideal quantum processes, denoted by $\mathsf{PTM}_{\rm proc}$ and distinguished here from algorithmic quantum Turing machines (QTMs). Coherent quantum processes extend strictly beyond this sector. The boundary is already visible in reversibility. Born-probability shadows of unitary gates preserve inverse composition exactly for basis permutations with phases. Outside this class, an exact positive stochastic simulation that supports universal quantum continuations must retain predictive information absent from visible probabilities. An inverse-recovery identity quantifies this phase ledger, and universal continuation forces the retained probability law to be tomographically sufficient for the quantum state. Under continuous full-state encoding assumptions, this requirement yields quantum-state dimension lower bounds. The familiar slogan $\mathsf{PTM}\subseteq\mathsf{QTM}$ is thereby sharpened into a precise classical boundary and a no-free-classicalization principle. Complete classical branching does not remove the predictive information needed to represent quantum coherence.

2610.22750.abstract_translated: 古典モデルがすべての分岐履歴と任意の因果記憶を保持できる場合、量子計算と古典計算を区別するものは何でしょうか? 我々は、正の因果履歴法則を記述する履歴解決型因果確率マシン (HCSM) を使用してこの問題を研究します。確率チューリングマシン (PTM) は確率アンサンブルモデル (SEnM) に埋め込まれ、SEnM はさらに HCSM に埋め込まれます。我々は、HCSM の履歴法則が、$\mathsf{PTM}_{\rm proc}$ で表される理想的な量子プロセスの固定基底、接頭辞保存対角セクターと完全に一致することを証明します。ここで、PTM はアルゴリズム量子チューリングマシン (QTM) とは区別されます。コヒーレント量子プロセスは厳密にこのセクターを超えて拡張されます。境界は可逆性において既に明らかです。ユニタリゲートのボーン確率シャドウは、位相を持つ基底置換に対して逆合成を正確に保存します。このクラスの外では、普遍的な量子継続をサポートする正確な正の確率シミュレーションは、可視確率には存在しない予測情報を保持する必要があります。逆回復恒等式はこの位相台帳を定量化し、普遍的連続性により、保持された確率法則は量子状態に対して断層撮影的に十分であることが強制される。連続的な全状態符号化の仮定の下では、この要件は量子状態次元の下限を与える。おなじみのスローガン $\mathsf{PTM}\subseteq\mathsf{QTM}$ は、それによって正確な古典的境界と自由古典化禁止原理へと明確化される。完全な古典的分岐は、量子コヒーレンスを表現するために必要な予測情報を除去するものではない。
2610.22750.title_translated: 量子計算の古典的境界：履歴解決型因果確率マシンと古典化のコスト

paper.title: Quantumness of Entanglement in Schwarzschild de Sitter Spacetime
paper.authors: Sumeng Wang, Xiaofen Huang
paper.abstract: We investigate genuine multipartite entanglement and genuine tripartite nonlocality of a noisy generalized GHZ state in Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime. The genuine multipartite concurrence and optimized Svetlichny parameter are employed to characterize these two quantum correlations. It is shown that the black hole and cosmological event horizons redistribute genuine multipartite entanglement differently among the physically accessible and inaccessible reduced states, while Svetlichny violation occurs only in the physically accessible state. We find that genuine multipartite entanglement can survive in the physically inaccessible states even when genuine tripartite nonlocality is absent. In addition, initial white noise suppresses both correlations, with Svetlichny nonlocality surviving over a narrower parameter region. Furthermore, in the Nariai limit, under the normalization adopted here, the correlations become concentrated in the physically accessible state. These results demonstrate the different robustness of genuine multipartite entanglement and genuine tripartite nonlocality under horizon effects and initial noise.

2610.22761.abstract_translated: シュワルツシルト・ド・ジッター時空におけるノイズのある一般化GHZ状態の真の多体エンタングルメントと真の三体非局所性を調査する。これらの2つの量子相関を特徴付けるために、真の多体コンカレンスと最適化されたスヴェトリチニーパラメータを用いる。ブラックホールと宇宙論的事象の地平線は、物理的にアクセス可能な縮約状態とアクセス不可能な縮約状態の間で真の多体エンタングルメントを異なる方法で再分配する一方、スヴェトリチニー違反は物理的にアクセス可能な状態でのみ発生することが示される。真の三体非局所性が存在しない場合でも、真の多体エンタングルメントは物理的にアクセス不可能な状態でも存続できることがわかった。さらに、初期白色ノイズは両方の相関を抑制し、スヴェトリチニー非局所性はより狭いパラメータ領域で存続する。さらに、ここで採用した正規化の下では、ナリアイ極限において相関は物理的にアクセス可能な状態に集中する。これらの結果は、事象の地平線効果や初期ノイズに対する、真の多体エンタングルメントと真の三体非局所性の頑健性の違いを示している。
